paper_metadata.title: Time series generation for option pricing on quantum computers using tensor network

summary: This paper proposes using matrix product states (MPS) as a classical generative model for Heston-model time-series generation, then uses the generated samples to price European, Asian, lookback, and up-and-out barrier options. With m = 6 and Dmax = 150, the MPS model reports prices of 1.0805 (European), 0.1915 (IV), 0.6107 (Asian), 1.4612 (lookback), and 0.9160 (barrier), compared with Heston benchmarks of 1.1098, 0.1967, 0.6195, 1.4778, and 0.9894, respectively.

experiments.description: Classical training of an MPS generative model on Heston-model time-series data, followed by classical Monte Carlo pricing of European, Asian, lookback, and up-and-out barrier options using samples generated by the trained MPS model; the paper discusses future quantum-circuit implementation but reports only classical numerical experiments.

algorithm.variant: Matrix Product State (MPS) generative modeling for time-series generation
algorithm.optimizer: gradient descent with sweeping algorithm (DMRG-like alternating optimization)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: run for multiple epochs; no explicit stopping criterion reported

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Each discretized asset price at each time point is mapped to an m-bit integer in {0,...,2^m-1}; the MPS is trained on these discrete symbols. The paper notes that such an MPS can later be embedded into a quantum circuit for state preparation, but no quantum circuit is executed in the experiments.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize negative log-likelihood L = -(1/|T|) sum_x log p_theta(x), equivalent to minimizing KL divergence between the learned distribution p_theta and the target discretized Heston distribution.

problem_instance.description: Heston stochastic-volatility model time-series generation for option pricing; generate discretized asset-price paths and price path-dependent options.

dataset_specification.description: Parameters: kappa=1.0, theta=0.04, xi=2, rho=-0.7; initial asset price S0=100, initial variance v0=0.04; Euler-Maruyama discretization with daily time step dt=1/250; path length M=5; 10,000 simulated paths for training and evaluation.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize each price using min-max scaling to m-bit integers: S_t -> floor((2^m - 1) * (S_t - S_min)/(S_max - S_min)); reflection positivity applied to keep variance nonnegative (nu_i = -nu_i if nu_i < 0).
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare MPS-generated path distributions and option prices against the original Heston-model Monte Carlo benchmark; 10 independent calculations for each option/model combination; report averages and standard errors.

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical Monte Carlo simulation for option pricing; Heston paths generated classically via Euler-Maruyama
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate Heston paths classically; discretize prices to m-bit integers; train MPS on 10,000 paths.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert generated integers back to real prices; compute European, Asian, lookback, and barrier option prices by Monte Carlo; compute implied volatility from European call price.

speedup_claims.conditions: when using quantum monte carlo integration with quantum amplitude estimation for option pricing
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this as a general QMCI/QAE complexity result (O(1/epsilon) vs O(1/epsilon^2)); it is not implemented in the reported experiments, which are purely classical.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: QMCI state-preparation step discussed as O(1/epsilon) for amplitude estimation-based Monte Carlo, but not implemented in experiments; MPS sampling/training complexity not given as a formal asymptotic bound.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical Monte Carlo option pricing scales as O(1/epsilon^2) for accuracy epsilon (as stated in the introduction).

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a fault-tolerant implementation of MPS-based state preparation plus QAE-based Monte Carlo; the paper does not provide qubit counts, circuit depth, or hardware resource estimates.
limiting_factors: State preparation is only discussed conceptually
Reported speedup is the generic quadratic QMCI/QAE scaling, not demonstrated
Classical Monte Carlo and MPS training/sampling are the only executed methods

notes: No quantum hardware or executed quantum circuit is reported; hardware.type is not_specified because the experiments are purely classical numerical simulations.
num_qubits is inferred as null because the paper discusses future quantum-circuit embedding of MPS but does not execute or size a quantum circuit in the experiments.
